record.excerpt: I run this system on 10 different time frames … the more time frames that align the higher the chance of success and the more money I make. … Except I use the lowest Moving average against Price … I determined the average price moves against its slowest tracking average by back testing.
record.performance_claim: the more time frames that align the higher the chance of success and the more money I make.
record.notes: MA system with no periods, asset or entry/exit; claims backtested edge. Compiler should refuse (no parameters).

spec.claim_summary: A system compares price to its slowest moving average across ten timeframes, with more aligned timeframes claimed to increase success.
spec.untestable_reason: No mechanical rule can be recovered because the moving-average lengths, trade direction, entry trigger and exit are unspecified and the core ten-timeframe alignment rule has no single-timeframe equivalent.
assumptions: No asset is named, so BTCUSDT is assumed as the default test asset.
No single timeframe is named, so 1d is assumed for a single-timeframe test.
No moving-average length, price-versus-average trigger direction, trade direction, or exit is specified.
NOT EXPRESSIBLE: alignment across 10 different time frames is the heart of the claimed edge and cannot be expressed in a single-timeframe rule.
